one_line: An overhead, hands-only demo of cutting a pineapple core into sticks for a 6 month old, followed by a clip of a baby chewing a stick and an end card promoting the Solid Starts app.

hook.visual: Overhead close-up of a light counter covered in pale-yellow pineapple slabs and sticks while two hands hold up one stick; a knife edge is visible at the left.
hook.on_screen_text: A pineapple core helps babies learn how to chew
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: It opens on the finished baby-food sticks already in hand and states a benefit tied to a milestone (learning to chew) in large white text that works muted. The 'core', the part most people discard, is the surprising ingredient (inferred).

beats.observed: Overhead shot of pineapple slabs and pale sticks on a counter; hands pick up and show one stick. Centred white text.
beats.on_screen_text: A pineapple core helps babies learn how to chew

beats.observed: Whole pineapple on the counter; a chef's knife slices off the top and the skin. At 6.0 s the cut end shows a paler round centre (the core, inferred), at 7.5 s a strip of skin comes off.
beats.on_screen_text: Here's how to prepare it for 6 month olds (at 3.0 s only)

beats.observed: Hands cut the peeled pineapple into thick slabs and then strips on a bare counter, with cut slabs left at the top of the frame. Hands and sleeve only, no face.

Hard cut to a baby in a high chair with a harness, bright window behind, holding a yellow stick to the mouth (13.5 s), gripping it (15.0 s) and chewing a shorter piece (16.5 s). The 16.5 to 18.0 s span is not sampled.

Plain white screen with a phone mockup showing the Solid Starts app page 'Pineapple', with a graphic 'How to Cut Pineapple for Babies' and the age steps '6 months+' (sticks or slice on the core), '9 months+' (bite-sized pieces) and '12 months+' (bite-sized pieces); a scroll shows photos of a wide slice and bite-sized pieces.
beats.on_screen_text: Learn more in the Solid Starts app!

beats.observed: Solid Starts logo in a dark navy circle: a beet, a cucumber slice and a bitten cookie icon above the words 'SOLID STARTS'.

payoff: The method is shown from 3.0 to 13.0 s and the proof (a real baby chewing a stick) lands at 13.5 s; the app pointer arrives at 18.0 s. The caption holds the safety answer, which the video itself does not show.
cta: On screen: 'Learn more in the Solid Starts app!' (18.0 to 19.5 s). In the caption: 'Does your baby have a favorite food teether?'
share_or_comment_trigger: Strong pass-along: 4,616 shares is about 28 percent of the 16,400 likes and 0.18 percent of 2,500,000 views, which fits a utility how-to sent to partners, grandparents or other parents who feed babies (inferred). The caption answers a safety worry (are food teethers safe), but comments are modest at 169.
why_it_worked: Breakout reach: 2,500,000 views is 276x the account median of 9,057, with a 0.66 percent like rate and 4,616 shares, which points to organic pass-along.
A concrete, saveable trick (use the core you would normally discard) opens on the finished product and a benefit line, so value is clear in under 3 s.
A real baby chewing the stick at 13.5 s gives proof and a payoff, and the caption answers a high-stakes parent fear (safety) in the search-friendly wording parents type.
paid_signal: no: like rate 0.66 percent is above the 0.3 percent flag and shares are very high relative to likes, consistent with organic spread; spend cannot be ruled out from the data.

solo_route.how: 1) Mount a phone on a tripod or a stack of books pointing straight down at a plain light counter, hands only in frame, and film how a LumeBook is made in 12 to 15 s: the photo upload on a laptop, the AI preview, then pages and the printed book (use a real sample book). 2) In CapCut or Canva, add a large 2 to 3 line white headline in the first 3 s with a benefit, then a short 'here's how it's made' line at about 3 s. 3) For the last 4 s, use a consented customer or ambassador clip of a child holding the book, or an overhead page-turn if none is available. 4) End on a clean white app or site screen and a logo card with one line and the website.
solo_route.needs: A printed sample book and the laptop preview screen. For the child reaction beat: a customer or ambassador clip with written parental permission; otherwise skip that beat.

lumebook_version.hook_he: ככה לומבוק הופך תמונה של הילד לספר אמיתי
lumebook_version.concept: A 15 to 20 s overhead, hands-only demo showing a child's photo becoming an AI-illustrated preview and then a printed book, with a big headline in the first 3 s and a consented customer clip of a child with the book near the end. Ends on a logo card and a site pointer.

evidence_notes: Whisper output is only '(upbeat music)' from 0 to 2.58 s, so there is no usable speech transcript; all beats are observed from frames at 1.5 s steps, and the unsampled 16.5 to 18.0 s span could hide a cut. On-screen text was read directly and is fully legible. The caption is a safety Q&A on food teethers (claims about 6 months and specialist experience) that the video does not itself show or prove. That the sticks are made from the core is inferred from the headline and the visible pale centre. The baby is not identified; the age is not stated beyond the '6 month olds' text. made_by is inferred from the brand account and the caption's 'we' voice.
